findings.F1: The next-day rebound after a fall depends almost entirely on whether volatility is rising. Here a fall means a day below −1 usual move, scaled by the prior 20-day volatility. The ratio used is 20-day over 120-day volatility, past-only, split into terciles. In the top tercile of that ratio the coin's next-day excess return is +1.47 % (t 4.42, 335 cases). In the middle tercile it is +0.28 % (t 0.98, 349). In the bottom tercile it is −0.15 % (t −0.68, 442).
findings.F2: In a regression of the next-day excess return on all 17 480 days, the interaction of fall depth with the volatility ratio is the strongest term. It scores −0.37 % per standard deviation with t −7.14. The fall depth alone scores t −2.43, the close location t −1.85 and the volume t 2.01.
findings.F3: When volatility is rising (top tercile of the ratio), deeper falls are followed by larger rises. Falls of −1 to −1.5 usual moves give +0.79 % (t 2.01, 162 cases), falls of −1.5 to −2 give +1.99 % (t 3.80, 84), and falls beyond −2 give +2.23 % (t 2.48, 89). In the bottom tercile the same depths give +0.28 %, −0.69 % and −0.40 %, with no grading.
findings.F4: The rising-volatility rebound holds across the sample. It is positive in all 8 years (+0.19 % to +3.54 %) and in all 6 coins (BTC +1.51 % t 3.18, XRP +3.50 % t 3.30, the others +0.90 % to +1.41 %). Its mean, +1.47 % per case, is about 7.7 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. The tested idea's unusual move is +0.19 %, only 1.0 times that cost.
findings.F5: The same split shows on the level of volatility within each coin. Falls below −1 usual move in the top tercile of the coin's own 20-day volatility are followed by +1.79 % (t 5.95, 607 cases). In the middle tercile the figure is +0.48 % (t 2.55, 679), and in the bottom tercile −0.20 % (t −1.39, 736).
findings.F6: Among falls below −1 usual move, a lower close in the day's range goes with a larger next-day rise: +0.91 % (t 4.17), +0.69 % (t 3.43) and +0.26 % (t 1.18) by close-location tercile, 674 cases each. This is the brief's absorption angle, but its spread is too small to stand out from the many angles examined.
findings.F7: The brief's own setup is heavy-volume, flat days (|z| < 0.5, top volume tercile). On those days the close location shows no link to the next day. The quintiles run from −0.76 % (t −1.47) to +0.31 % (t 0.85) with no order. The heavy-volume, low-close gain (+0.87 %, t 5.14) disappears outside falls (+0.20 %, t 1.09).
findings.F8: Weekday effects reverse between the two halves of the sample. Wednesday is −0.70 % (t −2.69) before 2022 and +0.10 % after; Thursday is +0.37 % before and −0.32 % after. They are not a pattern.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall in units of its 20-day daily volatility, the more the coin rises over the next day. The higher its 20-day volatility stands against its 120-day volatility, the larger that rebound.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a coin's falls on the next day mainly when its volatility has been rising, larger the deeper the fall and the higher the volatility ratio, and refuses such buys when its volatility is calm against its longer past.
ideas.name: rising-volatility fall rebound
